messages:
alex: Quick heads-up — ran a small ablation this morning around timing dithering on the continuous coalesce path. Results look interesting.
maya: Nice. Short summary?
alex: Baseline: microwindow_ms=10, coalesce_delay_ms=5, jitter=uniform(0,2ms). New: microwindow_ms=8, coalesce_delay_ms=3..7 jitter=exp(0,1.2) scaled. Also toggled kernel-v2 scheduling for long-token sequences.
sergey: Did you keep token_budget_target the same? That affects flush behavior.
alex: token_budget_target stayed at 128 for the run.
maya: What metrics did you collect?
alex: Collected p50/p95/p99 latency, batch size distribution, KV cache hit rate, and per-kernel time from the profiler. Quick numbers:

perf-bot: ```
baseline: p50=42ms p95=140ms p99=360ms  avg_batch=3.6  kv_hit=78%  kernel_long=28ms
dither-ablation: p50=39ms p95=128ms p99=345ms avg_batch=3.2  kv_hit=75%  kernel_long=30ms
``` 
alex: So p50/p95 improved a bit, p99 slightly improved but kernel_long increased ~2ms. KV hit dropped ~3pts.
sergey: small KV hit drop suggests earlier flushing causes less prefix reuse. Did you see more small batches?
alex: Yes — batch histogram shifted: +12% batches of size 1-2, -8% of size 4+. We think jitter shape made early arrivals more likely to flush.
maya: Any perf regression signals from CI or recent kernel bump that could explain kernel_long increase?
alex: The kernel bump to v2 happened yesterday on canary; I ran this ablation on the canary pool, so confounded. Kernel v2 seems ~+1.5ms on long-seq decode in isolation.
ton y: @alex can you paste the exact coalesce policy block you used?
alex: ```yaml
coalesce_policy:
  microwindow_ms: 8
  coalesce_delay_ms: {min: 3, max: 7}
  jitter: {type: "exp", scale: 1.2}
  token_budget_target: 128
  max_wait_ms: 120
```
sergey: Suggest trying token_budget_target=160 to recover KV hit and batch sizes; also try keeping microwindow at 10 but vary jitter distribution only.
maya: Agree. Also run a control on kernel-v1 so we can separate kernel delta from jitter effect.
devops: I can spin up two 1-hour runs on canary/v1 and canary/v2 with the same coalesce policy. ETA 40m.
alex: Thanks. Also logging note: add per-request kv_prefix_len to trace to verify prefix reuse hypothesis.
perf-bot: Action items: [alex] add kv_prefix_len trace, [sergey] test token_budget_target 160, [devops] run paired canary jobs, [maya] collect batch histograms and per-kernel times. Deadline: EOD.
maya: Small follow-up — if we increase token_budget_target, watch tail latency under bursty arrival patterns. Could get queue build-up.
alex: Yep will simulate bursty traces from prod-replay when validating.
sergey: If kernel v2 stays worse, file a regression with kernel/ops owner; but prioritize batching policy that preserves kv_hit while reducing p95.
alex: Thanks all. I'll post results in this thread when runs finish. :thumbsup:
